Find the nearest decision boundary for a single target observation

bl_find_local_cf.Rd

Searches across multiple component pairs for the closest decision boundary to the target observation in the rotated biplot space. For each pair, the loading matrix is rotated so that the target observation is aligned with the plane of that pair (see Rotation), then a fine grid is scored and the boundary contour is extracted.

Usage

bl_find_local_cf(
  bl_result,
  bl_target,
  set_filters = NULL,
  max_pairs = 21L,
  m = 200L,
  distance = c("auto", "mahalanobis", "euclidean"),
  verbose = TRUE,
  hull = TRUE
)

Arguments

bl_result

A "bl_result" object.

bl_target

A "bl_target" object from bl_select_target.

set_filters

A "bl_filters" object from set_filters, or NULL (no actionability constraints).

max_pairs

Integer; maximum number of component pairs to try. Default 21L: every pair for up to 7 features (choose(7, 2) = 21). With more features, the pairs with the highest components are left out.

m

Integer; grid resolution along each axis. Default 200L.

distance

Character; cross-pair selection metric. One of "auto" (default: "euclidean" for a PCA biplot, "mahalanobis" for a CVA biplot), "mahalanobis" or "euclidean". See Cross-pair selection criterion section above.

verbose

Logical; print progress messages. Default TRUE.

hull

Logical; keep only boundary points inside the convex hull of the training data and the target on each rotated plane (see Constraints). Default TRUE; FALSE searches without this rule.

Value

A list of class "bl_local_result" with the following fields:

B_z

1 x 2 matrix; the counterfactual in rotated Z-space: the best boundary point, or the projection of the restored or rounded point (see Fixed constraints and Integer features).

B_x

Data frame (1 row); the counterfactual in X-space: the back-projected boundary point, or the restored or rounded point.

B_pred

Scalar predicted probability at the counterfactual.

dist_z

Euclidean distance from target to boundary in the rotated Z-space of best_pair only (per-pair values are in all_distances). NA when no solution is found.

dist_x

Euclidean distance from target to boundary in X-space, each feature divided by its total standard deviation, for best_pair only (per-pair values are in all_distances_x). The selection criterion when distance = "euclidean". NA when no solution is found.

dist_mahalanobis

Squared Mahalanobis distance from target to boundary in X-space, for best_pair only (per-pair values are in all_distances_mahalanobis). The selection criterion when distance = "mahalanobis". NA when no solution is found.

distance

Character; the selection metric used ("mahalanobis" or "euclidean"), after "auto" is resolved.

Z_target

1 x 2 matrix; target coordinates in rotated Z-space.

best_pair

Integer vector of length 2; winning component pair.

Vr_rot

p x 2 rotated loading matrix for the best pair.

tVr_rot

2 x p inverse loading matrix for the best pair.

Z_train_rot

n x 2 matrix; training data in rotated Z-space.

Zgrid

Grid coordinates in rotated Z-space.

grid_prob

Numeric vector of model scores at each grid point.

col_value

Colour vector for grid points.

ct_local

Raw contour list from grDevices::contourLines.

xseq, yseq

Grid axis sequences.

min_val, max_val

Grid axis limits.

hull_polygon

Two-column matrix; the vertices of the convex hull on the plane of best_pair (rotated Z-space), or NULL when hull = FALSE or no solution is found.

all_distances

Named numeric vector; Z-distance per pair tried.

all_distances_x

Named numeric vector; X-space Euclidean distance (total-SD scale) per pair tried.

all_distances_mahalanobis

Named numeric vector; squared Mahalanobis distance per pair tried.

hull

Logical; the hull argument.

solution_found

Logical.

blocking_constraint

Character message if no solution, else NULL: why no boundary point satisfied the constraints, why the restored "fixed" point failed (see Fixed constraints), or why no whole-number candidate was valid (see Integer features).

bl_target

The "bl_target" object (the observed point).

bl_counterfactual

A "bl_counterfactual" object (the boundary point), or NULL when no solution was found. Mirrors bl_target: fields x_cf (1-row data frame, model units), z_cf, pred_prob (boundary probability), pred_class (from B_pred >= cutoff), and scaling. Its print method shows the counterfactual in original (raw) units when a scaling was set via bl_set_scaling.

bl_result

The "bl_result" object.

set_filters

The "bl_filters" object passed in, or NULL. Stored so that bl_find_sparse_cf can identify "fixed" variables and revert them to their observed values.

fixed_check

NULL when the search found no boundary point or moved no "fixed" feature. Otherwise a list: vars (the fixed features the search moved), applied (TRUE when the restored point is the counterfactual; FALSE when it failed, and then solution_found is FALSE), pred_restored (model probability at the restored point), in_range (whether it lies within train_ranges), and search_point (the search's own B_x, B_z, B_pred).

integer_check

NULL when no "integer" feature needed rounding (none is set, none moved, or the values are already whole), or when the search or the restore found no counterfactual. Otherwise a list: vars (the features rounded), applied (TRUE when a valid whole-number candidate is the counterfactual; FALSE when none was valid, and then solution_found is FALSE), n_candidates, n_valid, pred_rounded (the chosen point's prediction) and search_point (the point before rounding).

Rotation

The rotation adapts Biplot_rotation() from the research script (scripts/1.3 Optimal Rotation.R on the original_PhD_code branch of the repository). An SVD-based orthogonal rotation matrix \(A\) is computed such that the rotated loading matrix aligns the target observation with the projection plane defined by proj_pair. This gives each component pair the best possible chance of revealing a nearby boundary. Each pair of components labels one plane through the target point; since the Procrustes rotation turns the plane, the selected plane need not coincide with the plane spanned by the two components that name it.

Constraints

The convex hull polygon of the global biplot (from bl_build_grid()) is not used here, because the per-pair rotation invalidates its coordinates. Three constraint types are applied instead, in this order:

hull

When hull = TRUE (the default), a boundary vertex must lie inside the convex hull of the training data and the target, projected onto the rotated plane of that pair. The hull is rebuilt for every pair, as in Appendix A of the thesis, and applies its plausibility rule (section 4.3.1): the counterfactual is selected from a local decision boundary within the convex hull of the training data. hull = FALSE drops this rule.

set_filters

Actionability constraints supplied via set_filters.

train_ranges

Back-projected X-space values must lie within the per-variable ranges observed in the training data.

The hull applies to the boundary points on the plane. The restored ("fixed") and rounded ("integer") points lie off the plane, and are checked against the constraints and train_ranges only.

Fixed constraints

During the search a "fixed" feature may move by up to 0.5 in model units, because a vertex of the 2D boundary contour rarely holds a feature at exactly its observed value. After the best pair is chosen, each fixed feature the search moved is set back to its observed value and the point is re-scored. If the restored point still crosses the decision boundary and lies within train_ranges, it becomes the counterfactual (B_x, B_z, B_pred). Otherwise no counterfactual holds the fixed features, and none is reported: solution_found is FALSE, and blocking_constraint gives the fixed values the search reached, why the restored point fails, and that changing the constraints on the actionable features may make a counterfactual possible. Either way fixed_check records what happened. The restored point satisfies the fixed constraint exactly but lies off the 2D boundary, so it need not be the nearest valid point; the pair choice and the reported distances are those of the search.

Integer features

A feature marked "integer" in set_filters is searched as a continuous value, and rounded after the fixed restore. For each such feature whose counterfactual value is not a whole number in raw units, the whole numbers just below and just above are tried, and every combination of them is a candidate. A candidate is valid when the model still scores it on the other side of the cutoff, it meets every set_filters() constraint and it lies within train_ranges. The valid candidate nearest the target in X-space, by the same distance as the pair search (Mahalanobis, or Euclidean on the total-SD scale), is the counterfactual (B_x, B_z, B_pred); on a tie, the first. When no candidate is valid, no counterfactual is reported: solution_found is FALSE, and blocking_constraint says why and that changing the other constraints, or removing "integer", may make one possible. integer_check records what happened. Like a restored point, the rounded point lies off the 2D boundary; the reported distances are those of the search. Up to 12 integer features can be rounded together (\(2^{12}\) candidates).

Cross-pair selection criterion

The best component pair is selected by minimum distance from the target to the nearest valid boundary vertex, measured in X-space with \(v = B_x - x_{obs}\). Two distance metrics are available:

"mahalanobis"

Squared Mahalanobis distance using the within-class covariance matrix \(W\) stored on bl_result$metric_inv: \(d_M^2 = v^T W^{-1} v\).

"euclidean"

Euclidean distance with each feature divided by its total standard deviation (bl_result$X_sd): \(d_x = \sqrt{\sum_j (v_j / sd_j)^2}\), as dist_x in bl_find_boundary.

The default, "auto", follows the thesis rule (section 3.9.1): Euclidean distance for a PCA biplot and Mahalanobis distance for a CVA biplot. Under a standardised PCA the rotated loadings are orthonormal, so for the search's point on the plane \(d_x\) equals the 2D distance \(d_z = ||Z_{target} - B_z||_2\). Under CVA the loadings satisfy \(V^T W V = I / (n - g)\), every rotated basis inherits this, and so \(d_M^2 = (n - g) d_z^2\) for every pair: the Mahalanobis rule ranks the pairs as the 2D distance does. The two metrics measure the same way after the "fixed" restore and the "integer" rounding move the point off the plane. Within-pair selection (the nearest valid contour vertex) always uses 2D Euclidean distance in the rotated Z-space; only the cross-pair comparison and the integer rounding use distance. See documentation/biplot-rotation/biplot_rotation_and_pair_selection.md section 3.4 in the package repository.
